The IVAP multiprobabilistic fire test is a principled decision rule that transforms predictive distributions into actionable bets. It operates by checking three conditions: a minimum sample size (n ≥ 100), acceptable uncertainty (width OK), and a surplus over the observed odds (p_lo - q > τ). When all criteria are met, the model fires a bet; otherwise, it returns a NO_BET signal. This structure ensures that only well-calibrated, sufficiently supported predictions enter the live market, thereby enforcing honesty over volume. The test is derived from the duality between multiplicative forecast combination and conformal prediction, which provides finite-sample coverage guarantees even under adversarial betting pressure. Failure occurs when data sparsity triggers the sample-size check, causing the entire cascade to stall until more data accumulates.
